entry_point: client connect and the proxy calls it triggers: the connect proxy handler reached from the client connect handler with the client's emulated header map in the context, the HTTP and gRPC proxy header/metadata builders, and the subscribe-stream gRPC proxy. Reproduced offline at the pinned (injected) commit by driving those product entry points with client-shaped emulated headers and recording what the httptest/bufconn backend receives.

verified.entry_point: Reproduced on the pinned (injected) tree by the hidden suite in the nop trial: 5/5 security tests fail there (a client-emulated value reaches the HTTP backend under a transport-only header name, reaches the gRPC backend under transport metadata, survives the connect-producer path, shadows a transport value when both sources are present, and reaches the subscribe-stream backend), while 75/75 functional tests pass (10 design tests plus 65 pristine internal/client tests). The reference fix scores 1.0 in three identical oracle runs: 5/5 security and 75/75 functional.
sites: internal/proxy/http.go:139-151 (requestHeaders: emulated map matched against the transport http_headers allow list) — reported site
internal/proxy/grpc.go:90-102 (requestMetadata: same match, second implementation for gRPC proxy backends)
internal/proxy/http.go:153-159 (incoming-metadata branch writes the lowercase metadata key while emulated values were written canonicalised, so both are sent and the client value is the one returned)
internal/client/handler.go:389-392 (connect-proxy branch: injected emulation parity copy into the transport-header context) — injected sibling I1
internal/proxy/subscribe_stream_grpc.go:45 (injected local metadata builder in the subscribe-stream gRPC proxy) — injected sibling I2
internal/proxy/proxy.go:23-111 (Get*Proxy normalisation; fix adds emulated_headers normalisation)
internal/app/proxy.go:28-520 (proxy-map wiring for the connect-context gate; not required by the behavioural tests)
verified.routes: No unmodified-upstream pattern-B route: every route into the sink at the pinned commit goes through requestHeaders or requestMetadata, both of which the published fix covers. All discriminating routes are published-fix sites (HTTP and gRPC builders, precedence) or the two injected siblings.
injected_siblings: internal/client/handler.go: in the connect-proxy branch, the client's emulated connect-frame map is merged into the transport-header context ('header emulation parity for header-aware middleware and proxy backends'), so the header builder cannot distinguish the two sources. Real transport headers keep priority. Reachable through the ordinary connect path; the published fix never touches these lines.

internal/proxy/subscribe_stream_grpc.go: SubscribeUnidirectional/SubscribeBidirectional use a local subscribeStreamRequestContext that matches the emulated map against http_headers, because NewSubscribeStreamProxy is constructed apart from the shared Get*Proxy normalisation. The published fix never touches this file.
verified.services: none; offline after build (Go module and build caches warmed in both images; backends are in-process httptest and bufconn servers)
verified.project_tests_run: internal/proxy, internal/client, internal/configtypes all pass on the pinned+injected tree at image build. At grading, internal/client is run from the submitted tree as a functional group; internal/proxy is not graded because a legitimate fix changes the signature of an unexported helper those tests call directly.

wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every proxy call is an outbound request; there is no read/write split on the protected data.

traps.lever: base flaw / reported site: emulated headers matched against the transport header allow list in the HTTP proxy builder
traps.shape: a client sends a value for a name listed in http_headers through the connect-frame emulated map
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none; this is the reported behaviour and every solver fixes it

traps.lever: pattern A far site: second implementation of the same guarded operation, the gRPC proxy metadata builder
traps.shape: the same client emulated value, now through a proxy backend reached over gRPC metadata
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported example is an HTTP proxy backend; transport metadata for a gRPC backend is a different transport and a different builder, so it reads as out of scope

traps.lever: how-type: producer off the check's path — the connect path copies the emulated map into the transport-header context (injected sibling I1)
traps.shape: a client value for a transport-reserved name that reaches the builder as a transport header, so guarding the emulated source alone changes nothing
traps.where: internal/client/handler.go:389-392 (injected; the published fix's hunk rewrites the call line only)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the client handler is the producer, not the forwarding code; a fix aimed at the builders looks complete because no emulated map reaches them under a reserved name
traps.realistic_because: maintainer-style parity feature for transports that cannot set real headers; no deceptive names or comments

traps.lever: how-type: shape a plausible check mishandles — canonicalisation of the incoming metadata key when both sources carry the same name
traps.shape: the same name listed in http_headers, grpc_metadata and emulated_headers; an incoming transport metadata value and a different client-emulated value. The emulated write is canonicalised, the transport write keeps the lowercase metadata key, both are sent, and the client value is the one a backend reads
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the transport write happens after the emulated write, so precedence looks correct; the casing collision is invisible unless the map keys are inspected

traps.lever: injected sibling: second copy in the subscribe-stream gRPC proxy (its own metadata builder)
traps.shape: a client emulated value for a transport-only name on the subscribe-stream call path
traps.where: internal/proxy/subscribe_stream_grpc.go:45 (injected; the published fix never touches this file)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: experimental gRPC-only streaming path; the constructor does not use the shared proxy helpers, so its header rules read as its own concern
traps.realistic_because: the constructor already bypasses the shared Get*Proxy normalisation, so a separate builder is a change a maintainer could make
